# betteruptime_on_call_calendar (Resource)

https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/on-call-calendar/

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "betteruptime_on_call_calendar" "this" {
  name = "Terraform on-call calendar"

  # Tags whoever is on call as @terraform-example-on-call in each connected Slack workspace; "" stops tagging
  slack_group_handle = "terraform-example-on-call"
  # true would use a user group that already exists in Slack under that handle instead of creating one
  use_existing_slack_group = false

  on_call_rotation {
    # Replace with your team members' e-mails
    users             = ["petr@betterstack.com"]
    rotation_length   = 1
    rotation_interval = "day"
    # Midnight in the rotation's time zone; the offset fixes the first shift, the zone keeps that wall clock across daylight-saving changes
    start_rotations_at = "2025-01-01T00:00:00+01:00"
    end_rotations_at   = "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    timezone           = "Europe/Prague"

    # One block per day and window
    working_hours {
      day        = "monday"
      start_time = "09:00"
      end_time   = "17:00"
    }

    # Omit the times for a whole day
    working_hours {
      day = "saturday"
    }

    # Several blocks for one day are allowed
    working_hours {
      day        = "friday"
      start_time = "09:00"
      end_time   = "12:00"
    }
    working_hours {
      day        = "friday"
      start_time = "12:30"
      end_time   = "17:00"
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the on-call calendar.

### Optional

- `on_call_rotation` (Block List, Max: 1) Configuration block for the on-call rotation schedule. Ignored when omitted - on-call can be controlled in Better Stack. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--on_call_rotation))
- `slack_group_handle` (String) The handle of the Slack user group that tags whoever is on call in this calendar, without the `@`: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. Better Stack keeps the group's members in sync with the rotation. Set it to an empty string to stop tagging; leaving it out keeps the handle the calendar has.
- `team_name` (String) Used to specify the team the resource should be created in when using global tokens. You can't update this value later.
- `use_existing_slack_group` (Boolean) Whether `slack_group_handle` names a user group that already exists in Slack. `true` uses that group: Better Stack adds and removes only the people on call and keeps its other members. `false` creates a new group whose members are exactly the people on call, and a handle an existing group holds is refused. Leaving it out keeps the calendar's current choice (a new group if it has none).

### Read-Only

- `default_calendar` (Boolean) Whether the on-call calendar is the default on-call calendar.
- `id` (String) The ID of the on-call calendar.
- `on_call_users` (List of Object) Array of on-call persons. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--on_call_users))
- `slack_groups` (List of Object) How each connected Slack workspace took the handle. Groups are set up in the background after a change, so they read `pending` until it answers, usually within seconds. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--slack_groups))

<a id="nestedblock--on_call_rotation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `on_call_rotation`

Required:

- `end_rotations_at` (String) End time of the rotation in RFC 3339 format (e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`)
- `rotation_interval` (String) The interval unit for rotation_length. Must be one of: `hour`, `day`, `week`.
- `rotation_length` (Number) The length of each rotation shift. See `rotation_interval` for units.
- `start_rotations_at` (String) Start time of the rotation in RFC 3339 format (e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`)
- `users` (List of String) List of email addresses for users participating in the rotation.

Optional:

- `timezone` (String) Time zone the rotation's working hours are written in and its handovers follow across daylight-saving changes, an IANA name such as `Europe/Prague`. The offset in `start_rotations_at` still fixes the instant of the first shift, so write it in this time zone's offset. Omit to keep the time zone the rotation already has; a new rotation with working hours and no time zone uses UTC.
- `working_hours` (Block List, Max: 50) Windows during which the rotation pages anyone, one block per day and window. Omit for a rotation that is active around the clock; omitting it on an existing rotation removes its working hours. A window whose `end_time` is not after `start_time` runs overnight. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--on_call_rotation--working_hours))

<a id="nestedblock--on_call_rotation--working_hours"></a>
### Nested Schema for `on_call_rotation.working_hours`

Required:

- `day` (String) Day of the week. Must be one of: `sunday`, `monday`, `tuesday`, `wednesday`, `thursday`, `friday`, `saturday`.

Optional:

- `end_time` (String) End of the window as `HH:MM` on a 24-hour clock (e.g. `17:00`). Ends at midnight when omitted, so a block with both times omitted covers the whole day.
- `start_time` (String) Start of the window as `HH:MM` on a 24-hour clock (e.g. `09:00`). Starts at midnight when omitted.

- `phone_numbers` (List of String)
